title: F-16A Block 10/15 — Subsystems (Fuel/Avionics Volume, Landing Gear) vs Ground Truth
condition: Run at Brandt's own W_TO=31377.00 lbf, W_energy=6296.30 lbf (Wt!B3/B38, Wt!B6).
referenceDesc: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_subsystems_ground_truth.json (fuel/avionics volume, landing-gear tire diameter) and f16a_ground_truth.json .weights (fuel/avionics WEIGHT, cross-check rows only).
secondDesc: Nicolai & Carichner's independently-published "nose gear ~20% of TOGW" rule of thumb (p.202) -- a THIRD data point for the gear-load-split question, alongside Raymer's 90/10 (used) and Brandt's derived 26.7/73.3 (not used).

rows.notes: DEFINITIONAL, do not conflate: framework uses Raymer Table 11.6's 0.055 x W_EMPTY (an aircraft-empty-weight fraction); Brandt uses its own uncited 0.081 x W_TO (a takeoff-weight fraction) -- two different weight BASES from two different sources, not two estimates of the same formula. A large %Diff here is not a framework error to chase.

rows.cite: Brandt "Gear tab" (f16a_geometry.json gear block) -- UNDOCUMENTED cell reference
rows.notes: CAVEAT 1 (undocumented provenance): this Brandt figure's only citation anywhere in VnV/BrandtF16A is the JSON's own "_source": "Gear tab -- landing gear geometry", no cell letter/number; readme_geom.md's Input Schema and cell-map.md both omit it entirely. CAVEAT 2 (load-split contradiction): the SAME Brandt gear block implies a 26.7% main / 73.3% nose load split (see the Gear Load Split section below) -- a near-reversal of the Raymer 90/10 split this tire-diameter formula actually uses. Report this %Diff, but do not treat it as a clean validation.

rows.notes: Framework uses Raymer's stated typical fighter split (Ch.11 p.344 prose) as its DECIDED default, deliberately NOT the Brandt-derived figure -- VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md 2026-07-31 entry. The huge %Diff here is the expected signature of that locked decision, not a framework defect.

rows.parameter: Nose gear load, % of W_TO (framework default)
rows.notes: Mirror of the main-gear row above -- main_pct+nose_pct sum to 100% on both sides by construction.

rows.parameter: Nose gear load, % of W_TO, vs Nicolai's OWN rule of thumb
rows.cite: [Nicolai & Carichner, p.202]: "Nose gear rule of thumb: 20% of TOGW on the nose wheel"
rows.notes: A THIRD, independent data point: Nicolai's own repo-documented rule of thumb (20% nose) is exactly DOUBLE the framework's Raymer-derived default (10%), and both published-textbook figures disagree with the Brandt-derived 73.3% by an even larger margin. Worth a sanity check, though neither Raymer nor Nicolai claims a single point value for this design-dependent split.
